verdict.rationale: FFmpeg has no graphical UI. Its primary interface is a scriptable CLI ([ffmpeg-probe-4], [ffmpeg-docs-3]), and the same pipeline is exposed as documented libraries: libavformat, libavfilter and libavdevice ([ffmpeg-gh-3]–[ffmpeg-gh-5]), with Doxygen API docs ([ffmpeg-docs-10]) and coding examples ([ffmpeg-gh-6]). New capabilities such as IAMF land in both the library and the CLI ([ffmpeg-docs-14]), so nothing appears to be locked behind a non-programmatic interface. Community reports say the libav API documentation and examples are sparse and outdated ([ffmpeg-comm-11]) and that the C API easily allows invalid states ([ffmpeg-comm-17]); missing for 10: an explicit first-party statement of CLI-to-library feature parity, and richer, current API documentation and tutorials.
